answer: Sybil resistance bonds each identity to collateral and treats correlated equivocation as a coordinated fault: when k identities sign conflicting histories, the penalty grows as O(k^2), rather than as k independent fixed fines. Detection may also apply an exponential multiplier to capital loss, making a larger swarm disproportionately costly; escrow prevents operators from escaping by abandoning keys. A plume of evidence over a knoll can expose the shared thread of control, while unrelated honest keys avoid the group penalty.
